hypotheses.justification: This is the only argument of the theorem: the section variables {H}, [NormedAddCommGroup H], [InnerProductSpace ℂ H], [CompleteSpace H] are not mentioned in the statement (no `include`), so Lean does not add them, and `UniversalHyperreflexivity C` (Representation/Amplification.lean, line 237) is a closed `Prop` with no extra parameters. The hypothesis carries no mathematical content in this library, because `PublishedUniformInputs` is a closed proposition that is *proved*: `OAI.KadisonSimilarity.publishedUniformInputs : PublishedUniformInputs.{u}` (Representation/SeparableModelConstruction.lean, line 80, built from `exists_publishedSeparableModel`), with no hypotheses of its own (the ambient `H`-variables do not occur in its type, and the file contains no `sorry`/`axiom`). Hence deleting the argument leaves the statement `UniversalHyperreflexivity.{u} universalConstant`, which is exactly `OAI.KadisonSimilarity.universalHyperreflexivity` (UnconditionalMain.lean, line 23), itself the term `universalHyperreflexivity_of_published publishedUniformInputs`. Concretely: the current proof uses `inputs` only through `uniformCommutatorEstimate_of_published inputs`; replacing that term with `uniformCommutatorEstimate_of_published publishedUniformInputs` (equivalently, replacing the whole proof by `universalHyperreflexivity`) proves the residual statement. There are no degenerate/junk-value cases to check, since the residual statement is proven outright. Note: I am not claiming the hypothesis is unused in the existing proof — it is used at line 95 — only that the conclusion is provable without it, so the conditional form is strictly weaker than what the library already establishes.
